header.name: Real Analysis I
header.description: This course covers topics in real analysis of single-variable. The course starts with the concept of the real number system, and describes its properties. Then, the course develops sequences and series in detail. Following this, the concepts of limit, continuity and differentiability of real-valued functions of one variable are covered in detail with emphasis on rigour and proofs for these various topics. Finally, the course develops the theory of Riemann integration of one-variable real-valued functions.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students are familiar with the real number system, can determine convergence-divergence of sequences and series.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to construct epsilon-delta proofs related to limits and continuity.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to apply concepts of differentiability and Riemann integrability.

lecture_topics: Real number system and properties: Rationals, Irrationals, Well ordering Property, Supremum and Infimum, Completeness Axiom, Archimedean Property
Real number system and properties (Cont.): Decimal expansion, Density Property, Cantor set.
Topology of real numbers: Structure of open and closed sets in real line
Sequence and Series of real numbers
Bounded, Cauchy, Convergent, Divergent and Monotone sequences
Subsequences and criterion for convergence using subsequences
Sequence and Series of real numbers (Cont.)
Convergence, Divergence, Absolute and Conditional convergence of series
Limit and Continuity of real valued functions of one variable
Definition of limit and continuity (both epsilon-delta and sequencial definition and their equivalence)
Properties of continuous function (in particular, Intermediate Value theorem, Boundary Value theorem)
Differentiability of real valued functions of one variable
Chain rule for differentiable composite functions
Riemann Integration of real valued functions of one variables
Definition of Riemann upper and lower sum
Criterion for integrability using Riemann sums
Fundamental theorem of calculus and anti-derivatives

resources.title: Introduction to Real Analysis;  Robert G. Bartle, Donald R. Sherbert
K. A. Ross, Elementary Analysis: The Theory of Calculus, Springer
Walter Rudin, Principles of Mathematical Analysis, McGraw-Hill
